answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving a daily job quota. This bond requirement forms a trellis for growth: new agents can join, but each added identity ties up real capital. An attacker running 1,000 fake agents must immobilize $100,000 to capture their quotas. A chorus of accounts may echo the same claims, but the admission signal is locked funds, not a fresh username.
